newsitem.title: POLAND: Summit on Belarus suggested for Lisbon.
newsitem.headline: Summit on Belarus suggested for Lisbon.

text.p: Lithuania has suggested a regional presidents' meeting on Belarus's constitutional turmoil during next week's European security conference in Portugal, Poland disclosed on Thursday.

But Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski said he doubted tensions would be much eased by talks between Belarus's Alexander Lukashenko and the heads of state of his worried neighbours Lithuania, Poland and Ukraine.
"Democracy in Belarus is such an important matter that it cannot just be left up to President Lukashenko," Kwasniewski told reporters at a briefing on preparations for the Lisbon meeting.
"Lithuania just... made a proposal, which we will examine but over which I am sceptical, that the three presidents might meet with the president of Belarus who will be there," Kwasniewski said.
"I would not really see a good conclusion, or even much sense to such a discussion."

Kwasniewski, Lithuania's Algirdas Brazauskas and Ukraine's Leonid Kuchma have jointly called for a constitutional solution to the crisis in Belarus, where Lukashenko has now increased his powers through a referendum.
